16	// DefaultPublishTimeout bounds the wait for the broker's publish
17	// acknowledgment when Publisher.Timeout is zero. The bound matters because
18	// Entire connections reconnect forever and nats.go buffers publishes while
19	// disconnected: without it, a publisher holding an HTTP request or a message
20	// disposition would wait indefinitely behind an unreachable broker instead
21	// of failing over to its retry path (the caller's outbox, nak, or 5xx).
22	const DefaultPublishTimeout = 5 * time.Second
23	
24	// StartProducerSpan opens a producer span named name on tr, pre-tagged with
25	// the standard messaging attributes (system=nats, destination=subject) — the
26	// publish-side counterpart of [StartConsumerSpan]. Extra attrs are appended.
27	// The caller owns the span and must End it, and should Inject the returned
28	// ctx into the outgoing message so the consumer can re-parent.
29	func StartProducerSpan(ctx context.Context, tr trace.Tracer, subject, name string, attrs ...attribute.KeyValue) (context.Context, trace.Span) {
30		base := append([]attribute.KeyValue{
31			attribute.String("messaging.system", "nats"),
32			attribute.String("messaging.destination.name", subject),
33		}, attrs...)
34		return tr.Start(ctx, name, trace.WithSpanKind(trace.SpanKindProducer), trace.WithAttributes(base...)) //nolint:spancheck // the caller owns the span and Ends it
35	}
36	
37	// Publisher is the JetStream publish core shared by Entire's producers: a
38	// producer span, W3C trace-context injection, Nats-Msg-Id dedup, and a
39	// bounded wait for the broker's ack. Every service had grown its own copy of
40	// exactly this prologue around PublishMsg; Publisher owns the prologue and
41	// nothing else — subject construction, payload encoding, and the response to
42	// a failed publish (outbox retry, nak, HTTP 5xx) stay with the caller.
43	type Publisher struct {
44		// JS is the JetStream context to publish through.
45		JS jetstream.JetStream
46		// Tracer opens the producer span; nil uses the global OTel tracer
47		// provider.
48		Tracer trace.Tracer
49		// Timeout bounds the wait for the broker's PubAck; 0 uses
50		// DefaultPublishTimeout. It derives from the caller's ctx, so an
51		// already-cancelled ctx still fails fast.
52		Timeout time.Duration
53	}
54	
55	// Publish sends msg and waits — bounded by Timeout — for the broker's ack,
56	// wrapped in a producer span named "publish <subject>". A non-empty msgID is
57	// set as the Nats-Msg-Id header, the broker-side dedup key within the
58	// stream's duplicate window; empty leaves any Nats-Msg-Id already on msg
59	// untouched. Trace context from ctx is injected into msg's headers (msg is
60	// mutated) so the consumer span re-parents across the hop.
61	//
62	// The returned PubAck reports where the message landed and whether the
63	// broker deduplicated it (PubAck.Duplicate) — a duplicate is a normal
64	// outcome for an at-least-once producer retrying, not an error. The
65	// stream, sequence, and duplicate outcome are also recorded on the span.
66	func (p Publisher) Publish(ctx context.Context, msg *nats.Msg, msgID string) (*jetstream.PubAck, error) {
67		tr := p.Tracer
68		if tr == nil {
69			tr = otel.Tracer("github.com/entireio/go-nuts/natsmsg")
70		}
71		ctx, span := StartProducerSpan(ctx, tr, msg.Subject, "publish "+msg.Subject)
72		defer span.End()
73	
74		if msgID != "" {
75			if msg.Header == nil {
76				msg.Header = nats.Header{}
77			}
78			msg.Header.Set(nats.MsgIdHdr, msgID)
79			span.SetAttributes(attribute.String("messaging.message.id", msgID))
80		}
81		Inject(ctx, msg)
82	
83		timeout := p.Timeout
84		if timeout == 0 {
85			timeout = DefaultPublishTimeout
86		}
87		pubCtx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, timeout)
88		defer cancel()
89	
90		ack, err := p.JS.PublishMsg(pubCtx, msg)
91		if err != nil {
92			span.RecordError(err)
93			span.SetStatus(codes.Error, "publish")
94			return nil, fmt.Errorf("natsmsg: publish %s: %w", msg.Subject, err)
95		}
96		span.SetAttributes(
97			attribute.String("messaging.nats.stream", ack.Stream),
98			attribute.Int64("messaging.nats.sequence", ClampToInt64(ack.Sequence)),
99			attribute.Bool("messaging.nats.duplicate", ack.Duplicate),
100		)
101		return ack, nil
102	}

1	// Package backoff is the redelivery policy for transiently-failed JetStream
2	// deliveries: a NakWithDelay envelope — flat by default, optionally growing
3	// multiplicatively per delivery — bounded by MaxDeliver, with an optional
4	// Term on the final delivery.
5	//
6	// The Term-on-exhaustion posture is the COR-762 fix, lifted from
7	// mirror-pipeline's fanoutengine: on the final delivery a Nak is dropped
8	// silently by the broker (MaxDeliver reached), and on a WorkQueue stream the
9	// un-acked message then orphans — pinning the oldest-pending-age gauge — until
10	// StreamMaxAge finally expires it. Terming instead removes it cleanly. Streams
11	// where lingering is acceptable (a webhook stream whose max_age doubles as the
12	// retry backstop) leave TermOnExhaustion off and keep the plain Nak.
13	//
14	// The policy owns disposition only. Dead-letter capture stays with the caller,
15	// which should capture BEFORE disposing — gate it on [IsFinalDelivery]:
16	//
17	//	if backoff.IsFinalDelivery(msg, p.MaxDeliver) {
18	//		captureToDLQ(ctx, msg)
19	//	}
20	//	outcome, err := p.NakOrTerm(msg)
21	package backoff
22	
23	import (
24		"fmt"
25		"math"
26		"time"
27	
28		"github.com/nats-io/nats.go/jetstream"
29	)
30	
31	// Outcome is the disposition NakOrTerm chose, for the caller's metrics and
32	// logs.
33	type Outcome string
34	
35	const (
36		OutcomeNak  Outcome = "nak"
37		OutcomeTerm Outcome = "term"
38	)
39	
40	// Policy is the redelivery envelope a consumer applies to transient
41	// failures. MaxDeliver must match the consumer's on-server MaxDeliver — the
42	// policy detects the final delivery by comparing against it.
43	type Policy struct {
44		// NakDelay is the base delay before redelivery, and with a zero Factor
45		// the whole envelope: flat suits failures expected to clear on their own
46		// timetable, with MaxDeliver bounding the total.
47		NakDelay time.Duration
48		// Factor is the optional multiplicative growth per prior delivery: the
49		// Nth delivery naks with NakDelay × Factor^(N-1), capped at MaxDelay.
50		// Values ≤ 1 (including the zero value) keep the flat envelope. Growing
51		// envelopes suit failures that get cheaper to wait out than to retry —
52		// a downstream in a crash loop, a rate limit — where hammering on the
53		// flat cadence spends MaxDeliver too fast.
54		Factor float64
55		// MaxDelay caps the grown delay; it does nothing for a flat policy.
56		// Zero with a growing Factor leaves growth bounded only by MaxDeliver
57		// ending the redeliveries (the computed delay still saturates rather
58		// than overflowing).
59		MaxDelay time.Duration
60		// MaxDeliver is the consumer's redelivery cap
61		// (jetstream.ConsumerConfig.MaxDeliver). Non-positive means unlimited
62		// redeliveries — matching the jetstream field's semantics — so no
63		// delivery is ever final and NakOrTerm always Naks.
64		MaxDeliver int
65		// TermOnExhaustion makes the final delivery Term instead of Nak, so a
66		// work-queue message is removed cleanly rather than orphaning un-acked
67		// (COR-762). Callers with a DLQ capture before calling NakOrTerm.
68		TermOnExhaustion bool
69	}
70	
71	// NakOrTerm applies the policy to a transiently-failed delivery: NakWithDelay
72	// (see [Policy.DelayFor]) for redelivery, or — on the final delivery with
73	// TermOnExhaustion set — Term. Without TermOnExhaustion the final delivery
74	// still Naks; the broker drops the Nak at MaxDeliver and the stream's
75	// retention decides the message's fate.
76	//
77	// The returned Outcome reports which disposition was chosen, for the caller's
78	// metrics and logs. A disposition error is worth a log line but nothing more:
79	// a failed Nak redelivers via AckWait expiry anyway, and a failed Term on a
80	// work-queue stream means the message lingers exactly as it would have without
81	// the policy.
82	func (p Policy) NakOrTerm(msg jetstream.Msg) (Outcome, error) {
83		if p.TermOnExhaustion && IsFinalDelivery(msg, p.MaxDeliver) {
84			if err := msg.Term(); err != nil {
85				return OutcomeTerm, fmt.Errorf("term on final delivery: %w", err)
86			}
87			return OutcomeTerm, nil
88		}
89		if err := msg.NakWithDelay(p.DelayFor(NumDelivered(msg))); err != nil {
90			return OutcomeNak, fmt.Errorf("nak with delay: %w", err)
91		}
92		return OutcomeNak, nil
93	}
94	
95	// DelayFor reports the redelivery delay the policy applies after delivery
96	// number numDelivered (1 on first delivery): NakDelay for a flat policy,
97	// NakDelay × Factor^(numDelivered-1) capped at MaxDelay for a growing one.
98	// numDelivered ≤ 1 — including the 0 that [NumDelivered] reports when
99	// metadata is unavailable — reads as the first delivery. Exposed so a caller
100	// can log or meter the delay it is about to apply.
101	func (p Policy) DelayFor(numDelivered int) time.Duration {
102		if p.Factor <= 1 || numDelivered <= 1 {
103			return p.NakDelay
104		}
105		d := float64(p.NakDelay) * math.Pow(p.Factor, float64(numDelivered-1))
106		if p.MaxDelay > 0 && d >= float64(p.MaxDelay) {
107			return p.MaxDelay
108		}
109		if d >= float64(math.MaxInt64) {
110			// Uncapped growth outran time.Duration; saturate instead of wrapping
111			// negative (a negative NakWithDelay would redeliver immediately).
112			return math.MaxInt64
113		}
114		return time.Duration(d)
115	}
116	
117	// NumDelivered reports the JetStream delivery count (1 on first delivery), or
118	// 0 if metadata is unavailable (e.g. a synthetic test message).
119	func NumDelivered(msg jetstream.Msg) int {
120		if meta, err := msg.Metadata(); err == nil {
121			return int(meta.NumDelivered)
122		}
123		return 0
124	}
125	
126	// IsFinalDelivery reports whether this is the last delivery before JetStream
127	// stops redelivering (NumDelivered has reached MaxDeliver), so a transient
128	// failure here is terminal rather than another Nak-and-retry. A non-positive
129	// maxDeliver means unlimited redeliveries (the jetstream.ConsumerConfig
130	// semantics), so no delivery is final — without the guard the zero value
131	// would read every delivery as final and Term on the first failure.
132	// Unavailable metadata also reads as non-final: the safe default is another
133	// retry, not a Term.
134	func IsFinalDelivery(msg jetstream.Msg, maxDeliver int) bool {
135		if maxDeliver <= 0 {
136			return false
137		}
138		if meta, err := msg.Metadata(); err == nil {
139			return meta.NumDelivered >= uint64(maxDeliver)
140		}
141		return false
142	}

1	// Package jsconsumer is the durable JetStream pull-consumer scaffold shared by
2	// Entire's decode-and-dispatch consumers. Each of those used to hand-roll the
3	// same lifecycle: jetstream.New → CreateOrUpdateConsumer (durable, explicit
4	// ack, bounded ack-wait, bounded MaxDeliver, filter subject) → Consume → stop
5	// on context cancel; and the same per-message prologue: open a consumer span
6	// (re-parented across the NATS hop), decode the payload, and Term on a decode
7	// error.
8	//
9	// This package owns exactly that scaffold and nothing else. Each consumer
10	// keeps its OWN event type, business dispatch, metrics, and log lines — Start
11	// takes the consumer's message callback, and Process invokes the consumer's
12	// handle with the decoded event and the live span. The handler owns the
13	// message's terminal disposition (Ack/Nak/Term); Process never touches a
14	// message that decoded.
15	//
16	// Lifted from entire-api's internal/jsconsumer (COR-929), folding in the
17	// module's shutdown classification ([nuts.IsShutdownFetchErr] gates the
18	// consume-error log so a drain during rollout isn't reported as a fault,
19	// COR-923) and an optional [natsmsg.KeepInProgress] heartbeat for consumers
20	// whose handlers legitimately outrun AckWait.
21	package jsconsumer
22	
23	import (
24		"context"
25		"errors"
26		"fmt"
27		"log/slog"
28		"sync"
29		"time"
30	
31		"github.com/nats-io/nats.go"
32		"github.com/nats-io/nats.go/jetstream"
33		"go.opentelemetry.io/otel"
34		"go.opentelemetry.io/otel/codes"
35		"go.opentelemetry.io/otel/trace"
36	
37		"github.com/entireio/go-nuts"
38		"github.com/entireio/go-nuts/natsmsg"
39	)
40	
41	const (
42		// DefaultAckWait is how long JetStream waits for an ack before redelivery
43		// when Config.AckWait is zero — comfortably longer than an RPC round-trip
44		// plus a DB upsert, short enough that a stuck message redelivers promptly.
45		DefaultAckWait = 30 * time.Second
46		// DefaultMaxDeliver caps redelivery before JetStream stops redelivering a
47		// message when Config.MaxDeliver is zero.
48		DefaultMaxDeliver = 8
49	)
50	
51	// Config describes the durable consumer to create and how to trace/log it. The
52	// filter is given as either FilterSubject (single) or FilterSubjects (multi),
53	// mirroring jetstream.ConsumerConfig, so a migrated consumer preserves its
54	// existing on-server filter form exactly.
55	type Config struct {
56		Stream         string        // JetStream stream to bind (must already exist)
57		Durable        string        // durable consumer name, stable across restarts
58		FilterSubject  string        // set this OR FilterSubjects
59		FilterSubjects []string      // set this OR FilterSubject
60		AckWait        time.Duration // 0 → DefaultAckWait (see EffectiveAckWait)
61		MaxDeliver     int           // 0 → DefaultMaxDeliver (see EffectiveMaxDeliver)
62		SpanName       string        // per-message consumer span name (e.g. "repolifecycle.consume")
63		Name           string        // short consumer name, used as the log prefix
64	
65		// InactiveThreshold mirrors jetstream.ConsumerConfig.InactiveThreshold:
66		// how long the durable may go without an active subscription before the
67		// server deletes it; zero means never (the JetStream default for
68		// durables). Consumers on interest-retention streams set this so a
69		// decommissioned durable stops pinning every message it would have
70		// received, instead of holding them until the stream's MaxAge.
71		InactiveThreshold time.Duration
72	
73		// MaxAckPending mirrors jetstream.ConsumerConfig.MaxAckPending: the
74		// server-side cap on deliveries outstanding un-acked across ALL replicas
75		// sharing the durable; zero uses the server default (1000). Distinct
76		// from MaxMessages below, which caps only this process's client-side
77		// buffer.
78		MaxAckPending int
79	
80		// Tracer opens the per-message consumer span; nil uses the global OTel
81		// tracer provider.
82		Tracer trace.Tracer
83		// Logger receives the scaffold's own log lines (decode-term warnings,
84		// consume errors); nil uses slog.Default.
85		Logger *slog.Logger
86	
87		// KeepInProgress runs a natsmsg.KeepInProgress heartbeat while handle
88		// executes, for handlers that legitimately outrun AckWait. The extension
89		// is capped, so a wedged handler still redelivers — see
90		// natsmsg.KeepInProgress. The heartbeat stops when handle returns; a tick
91		// racing the handler's own terminal Ack/Nak/Term is a client-side no-op
92		// (nats.go marks the message disposed locally) that halts the heartbeat.
93		//
94		// Setting this forces the prefetch to one message (see MaxMessages): the
95		// heartbeat extends only the delivery the handler holds, so anything
96		// buffered behind a long handler would exhaust its AckWait unextended.
97		KeepInProgress bool
98	
99		// MaxMessages caps how many deliveries the consume loop buffers
100		// client-side (jetstream.PullMaxMessages); 0 uses the nats.go default
101		// (500). AckWait runs from server delivery into that buffer, not from
102		// callback dispatch, and callbacks run serially — so a consumer whose
103		// handler can approach AckWait should keep this small or queued
104		// deliveries expire and redeliver concurrently to other replicas.
105		// KeepInProgress forces it to 1; setting both to conflicting values is a
106		// Start error.
107		MaxMessages int
108	}
109	
110	// EffectiveAckWait is the AckWait actually applied to the JetStream consumer:
111	// Config.AckWait, or DefaultAckWait when zero. Use it — not the raw field —
112	// anywhere the real value matters, e.g. wiring a natsmsg.KeepInProgress
113	// heartbeat by hand (a zero ackWait there is a no-op).
114	func (c Config) EffectiveAckWait() time.Duration {
115		if c.AckWait == 0 {
116			return DefaultAckWait
117		}
118		return c.AckWait
119	}
120	
121	// EffectiveMaxDeliver is the MaxDeliver actually applied to the JetStream
122	// consumer: Config.MaxDeliver, or DefaultMaxDeliver when zero. Use it — not
123	// the raw field — when building a backoff.Policy for this consumer's
124	// messages: the two packages read zero differently (here it means "default
125	// to DefaultMaxDeliver"; on the policy it means unlimited redeliveries, the
126	// jetstream.ConsumerConfig semantics), so passing a zero Config.MaxDeliver
127	// through verbatim would make TermOnExhaustion never fire on the broker's
128	// real final delivery and orphan work-queue messages (COR-762).
129	func (c Config) EffectiveMaxDeliver() int {
130		if c.MaxDeliver == 0 {
131			return DefaultMaxDeliver
132		}
133		return c.MaxDeliver
134	}
135	
136	// validate rejects the configuration errors no retry can fix; shared by
137	// [Start] (one-shot) and [Run] (supervised, which must fail fast on these
138	// rather than retry them forever).
139	func (c Config) validate(nc *nats.Conn, onMsg func(jetstream.Msg)) error {
140		if c.KeepInProgress && c.MaxMessages > 1 {
141			return fmt.Errorf("jsconsumer(%s): KeepInProgress requires MaxMessages <= 1: the heartbeat extends only the in-flight delivery, so %d buffered messages would exhaust AckWait behind a long handler", c.Name, c.MaxMessages)
142		}
143		if c.Stream == "" {
144			return fmt.Errorf("jsconsumer(%s): Stream is required", c.Name)
145		}
146		if c.Durable == "" {
147			// CreateOrUpdateConsumer accepts an empty durable and silently makes
148			// an ephemeral, server-named consumer — losing the stable
149			// resume-across-restarts behavior this scaffold promises.
150			return fmt.Errorf("jsconsumer(%s): Durable is required", c.Name)
151		}
152		if onMsg == nil {
153			return fmt.Errorf("jsconsumer(%s): onMsg is required", c.Name)
154		}
155		if c.FilterSubject != "" && len(c.FilterSubjects) != 0 {
156			return fmt.Errorf("jsconsumer(%s): set FilterSubject or FilterSubjects, not both", c.Name)
157		}
158		for i, subject := range c.FilterSubjects {
159			if subject == "" {
160				return fmt.Errorf("jsconsumer(%s): FilterSubjects[%d] is empty", c.Name, i)
161			}
162		}
163		if c.AckWait < 0 {
164			return fmt.Errorf("jsconsumer(%s): AckWait must not be negative", c.Name)
165		}
166		if c.MaxDeliver < -1 {
167			return fmt.Errorf("jsconsumer(%s): MaxDeliver must be -1 (unlimited), 0 (default), or positive", c.Name)
168		}
169		if c.MaxMessages < 0 {
170			return fmt.Errorf("jsconsumer(%s): MaxMessages must not be negative", c.Name)
171		}
172		if c.MaxAckPending < -1 {
173			return fmt.Errorf("jsconsumer(%s): MaxAckPending must be -1 (unlimited), 0 (server default), or positive", c.Name)
174		}
175		if c.InactiveThreshold < 0 {
176			return fmt.Errorf("jsconsumer(%s): InactiveThreshold must not be negative", c.Name)
177		}
178		if nc == nil {
179			return fmt.Errorf("jsconsumer(%s): nil nats conn", c.Name)
180		}
181		return nil
182	}
183	
184	func (c Config) tracer() trace.Tracer {
185		if c.Tracer == nil {
186			return otel.Tracer("github.com/entireio/go-nuts/jsconsumer")
187		}
188		return c.Tracer
189	}
190	
191	func (c Config) logger() *slog.Logger {
192		if c.Logger == nil {
193			return slog.Default()
194		}
195		return c.Logger
196	}
197	
198	// isShutdownConsumeErr reports whether a consume error is the benign result
199	// of the connection going away during shutdown. [nuts.IsShutdownFetchErr]
200	// covers the core nats.go sentinels, but the jetstream consume loop surfaces
201	// its OWN [jetstream.ErrConnectionClosed] — a distinct value that wraps
202	// neither — so it must be matched separately or a clean rollout drain still
203	// logs a warning (the COR-923 noise this suppression exists to remove). As
204	// with the root classifier, it is only "clean" when ctx is already done; a
205	// mid-run connection loss is a genuine fault worth logging.
206	func isShutdownConsumeErr(ctx context.Context, err error) bool {
207		return nuts.IsShutdownFetchErr(ctx, err) ||
208			(ctx.Err() != nil && errors.Is(err, jetstream.ErrConnectionClosed))
209	}
210	
211	// Runner is a live consume loop. Stop halts it and is idempotent.
212	type Runner struct {
213		cc jetstream.ConsumeContext
214		// closed is cc.Closed(), captured while the subscription is live (the
215		// same channel is returned on every call, so capturing once avoids any
216		// post-Stop race) — it closes when the consume loop has fully wound
217		// down, including an in-flight handler.
218		closed <-chan struct{}
219		// watcherDone closes when Start's context-cancellation watcher exits. It is
220		// intentionally internal: callers synchronize on Stop, while tests pin that
221		// an explicit Stop does not retain a goroutine until the parent context ends.
222		watcherDone <-chan struct{}
223		stop        sync.Once
224	}
225	
226	// Stop halts the consume loop and blocks until it has fully wound down —
227	// including an in-flight handler — so a caller may tear down what handlers
228	// use (stores, publishers, the NATS connection) the moment it returns: the
229	// cancel → join → drain shutdown ordering (COR-923). Safe on a nil or
230	// never-Started Runner, idempotent, and safe for concurrent use — an
231	// explicit Stop can race the context-cancel stop armed by Start. Must not be
232	// called from inside the handler; it would deadlock waiting on itself.
233	func (r *Runner) Stop() {
234		if r == nil || r.cc == nil {
235			return
236		}
237		r.stop.Do(r.cc.Stop)
238		<-r.closed
239	}
240	
241	// Start creates/updates the durable consumer on nc and begins delivering
242	// messages to onMsg, returning a Runner that Stops when ctx is cancelled. The
243	// stream must already exist (provisioned declaratively); callers whose cells
244	// opt in per-stream gate Start behind that opt-in so a cell without the stream
245	// doesn't error at CreateOrUpdateConsumer.
246	//
247	// Consume errors are logged at Warn, except a drain/close during shutdown —
248	// both the core nats.go sentinels ([nuts.IsShutdownFetchErr]) and jetstream's
249	// own connection-closed error — which is a clean exit rather than a fault.
250	func Start(ctx context.Context, nc *nats.Conn, cfg Config, onMsg func(jetstream.Msg)) (*Runner, error) {
251		if err := cfg.validate(nc, onMsg); err != nil {
252			return nil, err
253		}
254		js, err := jetstream.New(nc)
255		if err != nil {
256			return nil, fmt.Errorf("jsconsumer(%s): jetstream.New: %w", cfg.Name, err)
257		}
258		cons, err := js.CreateOrUpdateConsumer(ctx, cfg.Stream, jetstream.ConsumerConfig{
259			Durable:           cfg.Durable,
260			AckPolicy:         jetstream.AckExplicitPolicy,
261			AckWait:           cfg.EffectiveAckWait(),
262			MaxDeliver:        cfg.EffectiveMaxDeliver(),
263			FilterSubject:     cfg.FilterSubject,
264			FilterSubjects:    cfg.FilterSubjects,
265			InactiveThreshold: cfg.InactiveThreshold,
266			MaxAckPending:     cfg.MaxAckPending,
267		})
268		if err != nil {
269			return nil, fmt.Errorf("jsconsumer(%s): create consumer %s/%s: %w", cfg.Name, cfg.Stream, cfg.Durable, err)
270		}
271		consumeOpts := []jetstream.PullConsumeOpt{jetstream.ConsumeErrHandler(func(_ jetstream.ConsumeContext, cerr error) {
272			if isShutdownConsumeErr(ctx, cerr) {
273				return
274			}
275			cfg.logger().WarnContext(ctx, cfg.Name+": consume error", slog.Any("error", cerr))
276		})}
277		switch {
278		case cfg.KeepInProgress:
279			consumeOpts = append(consumeOpts, jetstream.PullMaxMessages(1))
280		case cfg.MaxMessages > 0:
281			consumeOpts = append(consumeOpts, jetstream.PullMaxMessages(cfg.MaxMessages))
282		}
283		cc, err := cons.Consume(onMsg, consumeOpts...)
284		if err != nil {
285			return nil, fmt.Errorf("jsconsumer(%s): consume %s: %w", cfg.Name, cfg.Stream, err)
286		}
287		watcherDone := make(chan struct{})
288		r := &Runner{cc: cc, closed: cc.Closed(), watcherDone: watcherDone}
289		go func() {
290			defer close(watcherDone)
291			select {
292			case <-ctx.Done():
293				r.Stop()
294			case <-r.closed:
295			}
296		}()
297		return r, nil
298	}
299	
300	// isRetryableStartError classifies the narrow set of failures that can become
301	// healthy without changing Config or replacing nc. Everything else returns to
302	// the owner so a bad deployment cannot stay alive indefinitely with no
303	// consumer. Unknown server-side 5xx responses are retried, except known
304	// permanent JetStream configuration/account errors whose API happens to use a
305	// 5xx status.
306	func isRetryableStartError(err error) bool {
307		if errors.Is(err, jetstream.ErrStreamNotFound) ||
308			errors.Is(err, nats.ErrNoResponders) ||
309			errors.Is(err, nats.ErrTimeout) ||
310			errors.Is(err, nats.ErrDisconnected) {
311			return true
312		}
313	
314		var jsErr jetstream.JetStreamError
315		if !errors.As(err, &jsErr) || jsErr.APIError() == nil {
316			return false
317		}
318		apiErr := jsErr.APIError()
319		switch apiErr.ErrorCode { //nolint:exhaustive // unrecognized 5xx codes are deliberately retryable; all other unknown codes fail closed
320		case jetstream.JSErrCodeBadRequest,
321			jetstream.JSErrCodeConsumerCreate,
322			jetstream.JSErrCodeConsumerNameExists,
323			jetstream.JSErrCodeMaximumConsumersLimit,
324			jetstream.JSErrCodeJetStreamNotEnabledForAccount,
325			jetstream.JSErrCodeJetStreamNotEnabled,
326			jetstream.JSErrCodeConsumerAlreadyExists,
327			jetstream.JSErrCodeDuplicateFilterSubjects,
328			jetstream.JSErrCodeOverlappingFilterSubjects,
329			jetstream.JSErrCodeConsumerEmptyFilter,
330			jetstream.JSErrCodeConsumerExists:
331			return false
332		default:
333			return apiErr.Code >= 500
334		}
335	}
336	
337	// Retry envelope for [Run]'s supervision: exponential from runRetryInitial
338	// doubling to runRetryMax, reset once a consume loop survives longer than the
339	// max. Package vars (not consts) so tests can compress the schedule.
340	var (
341		runRetryInitial = time.Second
342		runRetryMax     = 30 * time.Second
343	)
344	
345	// Run supervises the consume loop [Start] builds. Where Start is one-shot —
346	// an error at consumer creation is returned, and a consume loop that closes
347	// underneath the caller (consumer deleted on the server, subscription
348	// invalidated) stays closed — Run retries both with exponential backoff
349	// (runRetryInitial doubling to runRetryMax, reset after a loop that outlives
350	// the max). In particular a stream that is not provisioned yet at boot — the
351	// declarative-provisioning race — is a retry, not a crash.
352	//
353	// Run blocks until ctx is cancelled, then joins the live loop (including an
354	// in-flight handler, see [Runner.Stop]) before returning, so it composes with
355	// the cancel → join → drain shutdown ordering as the body of a supervised
356	// goroutine:
357	//
358	//	g.Go(func(ctx context.Context) {
359	//		if err := jsconsumer.Run(ctx, nc, cfg, onMsg); err != nil {
360	//			log.Error("consumer config rejected", "error", err)
361	//		}
362	//	})
363	//
364	// Local configuration errors and permanent server responses (invalid consumer
365	// configuration, authorization/account setup) can never succeed on retry and
366	// are returned immediately. A missing declarative stream, temporary transport
367	// failure, or unknown server-side 5xx response remains supervised. A nil return
368	// means a clean, ctx-driven exit.
369	func Run(ctx context.Context, nc *nats.Conn, cfg Config, onMsg func(jetstream.Msg)) error {
370		if err := cfg.validate(nc, onMsg); err != nil {
371			return err
372		}
373		delay := runRetryInitial
374		for {
375			// Each attempt gets a child context so the cancel-watcher goroutine
376			// Start arms is released when the attempt dies, instead of one
377			// accumulating per recreate for the life of the process.
378			attemptCtx, cancelAttempt := context.WithCancel(ctx)
379			r, err := Start(attemptCtx, nc, cfg, onMsg)
380			if err != nil {
381				cancelAttempt()
382				if ctx.Err() != nil {
383					return nil //nolint:nilerr // a Start error during shutdown is a clean, ctx-driven exit, not a fault to report
384				}
385				if !isRetryableStartError(err) {
386					return err
387				}
388				cfg.logger().WarnContext(ctx, cfg.Name+": start consumer failed; retrying",
389					slog.Any("error", err), slog.Duration("retry_in", delay))
390			} else {
391				started := time.Now()
392				select {
393				case <-ctx.Done():
394					r.Stop()
395					cancelAttempt()
396					return nil
397				case <-r.closed:
398					cancelAttempt()
399					if ctx.Err() != nil {
400						return nil //nolint:nilerr // the loop closing during shutdown is the expected wind-down, not a fault
401					}
402					// A loop that ran long enough to be called healthy earns a
403					// fresh envelope; a flapping one keeps escalating.
404					if time.Since(started) >= runRetryMax {
405						delay = runRetryInitial
406					}
407					cfg.logger().WarnContext(ctx, cfg.Name+": consume loop closed; recreating",
408						slog.Duration("retry_in", delay))
409				}
410			}
411			select {
412			case <-ctx.Done():
413				return nil
414			case <-time.After(delay):
415			}
416			delay = min(delay*2, runRetryMax)
417		}
418	}
419	
420	// Process runs the per-message prologue shared by every consumer: open the
421	// consumer span (re-parented to the producer across the NATS hop), decode the
422	// payload, and on a decode error record it, log "<Name>: decode <Stream>;
423	// term", invoke onUndecodable (so the caller bumps its own drop metric with
424	// its own attributes), and Term the message — a poison payload won't decode on
425	// redelivery. On success it invokes handle with the span-enriched context, the
426	// live span (for RecordError/SetStatus on the business error paths), the
427	// message, and the decoded event; with Config.KeepInProgress set, an AckWait
428	// heartbeat runs for the duration of handle.
429	//
430	// Callers wire Process as the func they pass to Start AND the entry point
431	// their tests drive, so the decode-or-term path is exercised the same way in
432	// production and tests.
433	func Process[E any](
434		ctx context.Context,
435		msg jetstream.Msg,
436		cfg Config,
437		decode func([]byte) (E, error),
438		handle func(ctx context.Context, span trace.Span, msg jetstream.Msg, ev E),
439		onUndecodable func(ctx context.Context),
440	) {
441		ctx, span := natsmsg.StartConsumerSpan(ctx, cfg.tracer(), msg, cfg.SpanName)
442		defer span.End()
443	
444		ev, err := decode(msg.Data())
445		if err != nil {
446			span.RecordError(err)
447			span.SetStatus(codes.Error, "decode")
448			cfg.logger().WarnContext(ctx, cfg.Name+": decode "+cfg.Stream+"; term",
449				slog.Any("error", err), slog.String("subject", msg.Subject()))
450			if onUndecodable != nil {
451				onUndecodable(ctx)
452			}
453			if termErr := msg.Term(); termErr != nil {
454				cfg.logger().WarnContext(ctx, cfg.Name+": term failed", slog.Any("error", termErr))
455			}
456			return
457		}
458		if cfg.KeepInProgress {
459			stop := natsmsg.KeepInProgress(msg.InProgress, cfg.EffectiveAckWait())
460			defer stop()
461		}
462		handle(ctx, span, msg, ev)
463	}

5		"fmt"

13	// dlqPublishTimeout bounds one dead-letter PublishMsg. The consume context has
14	// no deadline, and PublishMsg waits for the PubAck indefinitely; without a
15	// bound a NATS blip would hang the handler (and, since a one-in-flight consumer
16	// keeps a slot occupied, stall the consumer) instead of failing the capture
17	// loudly.
18	const dlqPublishTimeout = 15 * time.Second
19	
20	// DLQ provenance headers added to the captured copy so a replay tool (or a
21	// human) can see why and from where a message was dead-lettered.
22	const (
23		DLQReasonHeader    = "Nats-Dlq-Reason"
24		DLQOriginHeader    = "Nats-Dlq-Origin-Subject"
25		DLQDeliveredHeader = "Nats-Dlq-Delivered"
26		DLQStreamSeqHeader = "Nats-Dlq-Stream-Seq"
27	)
28	
29	// DLQPublisher is the publish surface DeadLetter needs — satisfied by
30	// nats.JetStreamContext. Kept minimal so wiring can hand it the same
31	// JetStreamContext the per-cell publishers already hold, and tests can stub it.
32	type DLQPublisher interface {
33		PublishMsg(m *nats.Msg, opts ...nats.PubOpt) (*nats.PubAck, error)
34	}
35	
36	// SubjectToken sanitizes s into a single valid NATS subject token. NATS tokens
37	// cannot contain spaces, dots, or wildcards, so every character outside
38	// [a-z0-9_-] is replaced with '_' (and letters are lowercased). Use it to turn a
39	// human-readable dead-letter reason ("bad completion payload") into a subject
40	// token ("bad_completion_payload") — publishing to an unsanitized reason would
41	// fail, so the caller would never Ack the poison off a WorkQueue.
42	func SubjectToken(s string) string {
43		// Iterate bytes, not runes: we only keep ASCII [a-z0-9_-] and map everything
44		// else (including every byte of a multi-byte rune) to '_', so a byte loop is
45		// both correct and free of a rune->byte narrowing conversion.
46		b := make([]byte, 0, len(s))
47		for i := range len(s) {
48			c := s[i]
49			switch {
50			case c >= 'a' && c <= 'z', c >= '0' && c <= '9', c == '_', c == '-':
51				b = append(b, c)
52			case c >= 'A' && c <= 'Z':
53				b = append(b, c-'A'+'a')
54			default:
55				b = append(b, '_')
56			}
57		}
58		if len(b) == 0 {
59			return "unknown"
60		}
61		return string(b)
62	}

64	// DeadLetter republishes a poison message to dlqSubject, preserving its payload
65	// and headers and adding Nats-Dlq-* provenance (reason, origin subject,
66	// delivery count, stream sequence).
67	//
68	// It is the capture step a consumer runs before giving up on a message it can
69	// never process. DeadLetter copies the poison to a durable DLQ subject so it can
70	// be inspected or replayed, and the caller then removes the original from the
71	// stream — a Term on the final delivery (see backoff.Policy.TermOnExhaustion,
72	// whose doc notes callers "DLQ capture before calling NakOrTerm") or a plain
73	// Ack. Without this step a Term'd or MaxDeliver-exhausted message is discarded
74	// with no trail; DeadLetter is what makes the give-up auditable and recoverable.
75	//
76	// Returns an error if the republish fails; on error the caller MUST NOT remove
77	// the original — Nak or leave it so the poison is never dropped without a
78	// captured copy. Publishing is bounded by dlqPublishTimeout regardless of ctx's
79	// deadline.
80	func DeadLetter(ctx context.Context, pub DLQPublisher, dlqSubject string, msg jetstream.Msg, reason string) error {
81		hdr := nats.Header{}
82		for k, v := range msg.Headers() {
83			hdr[k] = append([]string(nil), v...)
84		}
85		hdr.Set(DLQReasonHeader, reason)
86		hdr.Set(DLQOriginHeader, msg.Subject())
87		if meta, err := msg.Metadata(); err == nil && meta != nil {
88			hdr.Set(DLQDeliveredHeader, strconv.FormatUint(meta.NumDelivered, 10))
89			hdr.Set(DLQStreamSeqHeader, strconv.FormatUint(meta.Sequence.Stream, 10))
90		}
91	
92		out := &nats.Msg{Subject: dlqSubject, Data: msg.Data(), Header: hdr}
93	
94		pubCtx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, dlqPublishTimeout)
95		defer cancel()
96		if _, err := pub.PublishMsg(out, nats.Context(pubCtx)); err != nil {
97			return fmt.Errorf("dead-letter publish to %q: %w", dlqSubject, err)
98		}
99		return nil
100	}

12	// keepInProgressMaxTicks caps the total AckWait extension at ~5×AckWait
13	// (ticks fire at AckWait/3). The heartbeat exists so a long handler that IS
14	// making progress — a whole-installation teardown fan-out, a multi-GB
15	// data-plane purge — doesn't get redelivered into a concurrent duplicate;
16	// it must NOT remove the broker's liveness failsafe entirely, or a wedged
17	// handler (hung I/O with no deadline) would pin its delivery to the wedged
18	// replica forever. Past the cap the extension stops and AckWait expiry
19	// redelivers to a healthy replica sharing the durable.
20	const keepInProgressMaxTicks = 15
21	
22	// isPermanentInProgressErr reports whether an InProgress failure can never
23	// succeed on a later tick: the delivery was already terminally disposed (an
24	// Ack/Nak/Term racing the heartbeat) or carries no JetStream reply subject to
25	// extend. Both the jetstream and legacy *nats.Msg sentinel values are
26	// matched, since the callback may wrap either message type. Anything else —
27	// a reconnect-buffer overflow, a flush timeout — can recover once the
28	// connection does, so the heartbeat keeps trying until the tick cap.
29	func isPermanentInProgressErr(err error) bool {
30		return errors.Is(err, jetstream.ErrMsgAlreadyAckd) ||
31			errors.Is(err, jetstream.ErrMsgNoReply) ||
32			errors.Is(err, nats.ErrMsgAlreadyAckd) ||
33			errors.Is(err, nats.ErrMsgNoReply)
34	}

36	// KeepInProgress calls inProgress at ackWait/3 until stop is called, resetting
37	// the broker's redelivery timer while a long handler runs. The extension is
38	// capped (keepInProgressMaxTicks) — see the constant for why.
39	//
40	// inProgress wraps the message's InProgress call — func() error { return
41	// msg.InProgress() } — for either jetstream.Msg or the legacy *nats.Msg.
42	//
43	// A failing tick stops the heartbeat only when the failure is permanent
44	// (already disposed, no reply subject — see isPermanentInProgressErr);
45	// a transient failure such as a NATS blip keeps ticking, bounded by the
46	// cap, so one dropped extension during a reconnect doesn't silently
47	// forfeit the rest of the handler's runway and invite a concurrent
48	// redelivery mid-run.

51	// consumer configs default it) returns a no-op stop.
52	//
53	// stop is idempotent and blocks until the ticker goroutine has exited, so
54	// no InProgress can race a terminal disposition (Ack/Nak/Term) issued
55	// after it returns.
56	func KeepInProgress(inProgress func() error, ackWait time.Duration) (stop func()) {
57		interval := ackWait / 3
58		if interval <= 0 {
59			return func() {}
60		}
61		done := make(chan struct{})
62		finished := make(chan struct{})
63		go func() {
64			defer close(finished)
65			ticker := time.NewTicker(interval)
66			defer ticker.Stop()
67			for ticks := 0; ; {
68				select {
69				case <-done:
70					return
71				case <-ticker.C:
72					ticks++
73					if ticks > keepInProgressMaxTicks {
74						return
75					}
76					if err := inProgress(); err != nil && isPermanentInProgressErr(err) {
77						// A delivery that can't be extended won't start
78						// succeeding on a later tick; stop instead of
79						// spinning. The real failure surfaces on the
80						// terminal Ack/Nak/Term.
81						return
82					}
83				}
84			}
85		}()
86		var once sync.Once
87		return func() {
88			once.Do(func() { close(done) })
89			<-finished
90		}

# natspub callers in mirror-pipeline — findings for the shared `Publisher` API

## The shared core being mirrored

`internal/natspub/natspub.go` defines the contract every caller uses. Key facts (confirming what you read):

- **Legacy JetStream only.** The publisher interface is the classic `nats.JetStreamContext` shape, and `Publish` calls `PublishMsg` with a `nats.Context` timeout. No modern `jetstream.JetStream` anywhere on the publish path (see section 3).
  - `natspub.go:37-40` — `type JetStreamPublisher interface { PublishMsg(m *nats.Msg, opts ...nats.PubOpt) (*nats.PubAck, error) }`
  - `natspub.go:109-111` — `pubCtx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, AckWait); ... ack, err := js.PublishMsg(msg, nats.Context(pubCtx))`
- `natspub.go:35` — `const AckWait = 5 * time.Second`
- `natspub.go:26` — `const MsgIDHeader = "Nats-Msg-Id"`
- The `Publication` struct (`natspub.go:44-68`) has exactly the fields you listed: `Tracer`, `SpanName`, `ErrKind`, `LogMsg`, `Subject`, `MsgID`, `Marshal func() ([]byte, error)`, `SpanAttrs []attribute.KeyValue`, `LogAttrs []slog.Attr`.
- `Publish` (`natspub.go:80-131`) prepends a fixed messaging.* triplet to `SpanAttrs`, starts a `SpanKindProducer` span on `otel.Tracer(pub.Tracer)`, runs `Marshal` **inside** the span, sets the `Nats-Msg-Id` header, calls `otelnats.Inject(ctx, msg)`, publishes, then stamps `messaging.nats.sequence` / `messaging.nats.duplicate` and logs one INFO line.
- Helper `natspub.PlacementAttrs(jurisdiction, cluster)` (`natspub.go:72-77`) returns `entire.target_jurisdiction` + `entire.target_cluster_id`.

## 1. The callers of `natspub.Publish` / `natspub.Publication`

There are **six** call sites of `natspub.Publish`, all constructing a `natspub.Publication` literal. Each typed publisher is a thin `Publisher{ js JetStreamPublisher }` wrapper (`JetStreamPublisher = natspub.JetStreamPublisher`, `NatsMsgIDHeader = natspub.MsgIDHeader`), delegating mechanics to natspub and owning only the domain parts.

| Package (file:line) | Tracer | SpanName (caller-selected op name) | ErrKind | LogMsg |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `pkg/metajobs/publisher.go:31` | `"metajobs"` | `"github_meta.publish"` | `"meta job"` | `"Published github_meta job"` |
| `pkg/prjobs/publisher.go:31` | `"prjobs"` | `"github_pr.publish"` | `"pr job"` | `"Published github_pr job"` |
| `pkg/pushauthorjobs/publisher.go:34` | `"core-fanout"` | `"github_push_author.publish"` | `"push-author job"` | `"Published github_push_author job"` |
| `pkg/donejobs/publisher.go:31` | `"donejobs"` | `"mirror.done.publish"` | `"done job"` | `"Published mirror completion"` |
| `internal/mirrorjobs/publisher.go:40` | `"mirrorjobs"` | `"mirror.git.publish"` | `"git mirror job"` | `"Published git mirror job"` |
| `pkg/webhookevents/publisher.go:89` | `"webhookevents"` | `"webhook.publish"` | `"forwarded webhook"` | `"Published forwarded webhook"` |

Note two things the shared API must accommodate:
- **Tracer name is not always the package name.** `pushauthorjobs` sets `Tracer: "core-fanout"` (the binary/scope name), while its `SpanName` is `"github_push_author.publish"`. Tracer and SpanName are fully independent, caller-chosen strings.
- **SpanName conventions vary**: dotted domain names like `github_meta.publish`, `mirror.done.publish`, `mirror.git.publish`, `webhook.publish`. All are literal strings passed straight to `otel.Tracer(Tracer).Start(ctx, SpanName, ...)`.

### Representative construction details

**metajobs** (`pkg/metajobs/publisher.go:30-42`) — the canonical placement-scoped shape:
```go
func (p *Publisher) PublishMetaJob(ctx context.Context, jurisdiction, cluster string, job Job) error {
	return natspub.Publish(ctx, p.js, natspub.Publication{
		Tracer:    tracerName,               // "metajobs"
		SpanName:  "github_meta.publish",
		ErrKind:   "meta job",
		LogMsg:    "Published github_meta job",
		Subject:   Subject(jurisdiction, cluster),
		MsgID:     MsgID(job.GitHubRepoID, job.ObservedAt),
		Marshal:   func() ([]byte, error) { return Marshal(job) },
		SpanAttrs: append(natspub.PlacementAttrs(jurisdiction, cluster), job.SpanAttrs()...),
		LogAttrs:  job.LogAttrs(),
	})
}
```
- **Subject** (`pkg/metajobs/jobs.go:62-64`): `SubjectPrefix + jurisdiction + "." + cluster`.
- **MsgID** (`jobs.go:115-117`): `strconv.FormatInt(githubRepoID,10) + "/" + observedAt.UTC().Format(time.RFC3339Nano)` — stable across redeliveries so republishes collapse in the dedup window.
- **Marshal**: closure over `Marshal(job)` which stamps schema version, validates, then `json.Marshal`.
- **SpanAttrs**: `PlacementAttrs(...)` **appended with** `job.SpanAttrs()` (`jobs.go:171-177`: `entire.target_ulid`, `entire.github_repo_id`, `entire.source_repo`).
- **LogAttrs** (`jobs.go:180-186`): unprefixed counterparts `target_ulid`, `github_repo_id`, `source_repo`.

**pushauthorjobs** (`pkg/pushauthorjobs/publisher.go:33-52`) — shows a caller building `SpanAttrs`/`LogAttrs` **inline** rather than from job methods, and mixing attribute types:
```go

	Tracer:   tracerName,                       // "core-fanout"
	SpanName: "github_push_author.publish",
	ErrKind:  "push-author job",
	LogMsg:   "Published github_push_author job",
	Subject:  Subject(jurisdiction, cluster),
```

```go
	Tracer:    tracerName,               // "mirrorjobs"
	SpanName:  "mirror.git.publish",
	ErrKind:   "git mirror job",
```

- `ErrKind` and `LogMsg` as free strings.
- `Subject` fully resolved caller-side (placement concatenation, or `gitjobs.Subject(parsed)`, or `Subject(event)`).
- `MsgID` derived caller-side by many strategies: numeric-id/timestamp, `a/b` concatenation, 5-part `fmt.Sprintf`, or a bare delivery id.
- `Marshal` as a closure (may stamp version + validate before JSON, or plain `json.Marshal`).
- `SpanAttrs` as an arbitrary `[]attribute.KeyValue` (String/Int64/Int seen), sometimes `PlacementAttrs(...)`-based, sometimes subject-derived, sometimes fully inline. `LogAttrs` as arbitrary `[]slog.Attr`.
- The helper `PlacementAttrs(jurisdiction, cluster)` is shared by the four placement-scoped publishers; the other two don't use it. Worth carrying into the shared API as an optional helper, not a required field.

## 2. `pkg/otelnats` vs go-nuts `natsmsg`

**mirror-pipeline `pkg/otelnats/nats.go`** (`otelnats.Inject`, lines 39-44):
```go
func Inject(ctx context.Context, msg *nats.Msg) {
	if msg.Header == nil {
		msg.Header = nats.Header{}
	}
	otel.GetTextMapPropagator().Inject(ctx, HeaderCarrier(msg.Header))
}
```
It adapts `nats.Header` to `propagation.TextMapCarrier` via `HeaderCarrier` (Get/Set/Keys). `Extract` (lines 48-53) does the mirror. This is the only otelnats helper on the publish path — `natspub.Publish` calls `otelnats.Inject(ctx, msg)` at `natspub.go:106`, right after setting the `Nats-Msg-Id` header. No other otelnats helper is used when publishing (Extract is consumer-side).

**go-nuts `natsmsg/tracecontext.go`** (`Inject`, lines 58-63) is **byte-for-byte the same body** — identical `HeaderCarrier` Get/Set/Keys and the same `Inject` implementation. The go-nuts package is the superset/unification (its doc at `tracecontext.go:1-10` says it unifies entire-core's `internal/natsmsg` and entire-api's `internal/otelnats`, "itself ported from mirror-pipeline"; tracking COR-929). 1. **`natsmsg.HeaderCarrier` additionally implements `propagation.ValuesGetter`** via `Values(key)` (`tracecontext.go:38-41`, asserted at `:51-54`). - Direct `PublishMsg` callers outside natspub: `pkg/webhookdlq/publisher.go:127`, `cmd/rekicker/rekick.go:63,223`, `cmd/meta-fanout/{lifecycle.go:156,backfill.go:97,backfill_prs.go:85}`, `cmd/mirror-pipeline-admin/{rekick.go:109,dlq.go:387}`. All legacy.

**Consumer-side redelivery/backoff = `pkg/fanoutengine/engine.go`** (this is the COR-762 work). The engine is explicitly kept "on the current legacy `nats.JetStreamContext` API" (`engine.go:11-13`); it holds a `js nats.JetStreamContext` (`:216`) and subscribes via `js.PullSubscribe(...)` (`:299`).

- **Subscribe-retry backoff** (`engine.go:40-45`, `:307-313`): `backoffInit = 1s`, `backoffMax = 30s`, doubling `backoff = min(backoff*2, backoffMax)` between failed `PullSubscribe` attempts.


- **`isFinalDelivery`** (`:717-722`): `meta.NumDelivered >= uint64(maxDeliver)`.
- **`TermOnExhaustion`** (Config field, `:193-198`) is the COR-762 fix: on a **work-queue** stream a Nak on the final delivery leaves the message un-acked and orphaned until `max_age`, so instead the engine `Term()`s on exhaustion (reason `max_deliveries`) even without a DLQ. ### Bottom line for the shared API design
- The shared `Publisher`/`Publication` must keep `Tracer` and `SpanName` as **independent free strings** (pushauthorjobs proves they diverge) and `SpanAttrs`/`LogAttrs` as **fully caller-assembled slices** (mirrorjobs and webhookevents don't use `PlacementAttrs`). # COR-984 — go-nuts Phase 2: deepen publishing & redelivery APIs

## Context

Phase 1 (COR-929) established the go-nuts lifecycle baseline and shipped `v0.7.0`
into mirror-pipeline, entire-api, and entiredb — but those repos only adopted the
`natsmsg` trace-context + DeadLetter helpers. The two seams Phase 3 will actually
converge — **publishing** (`natsmsg.Publisher`) and **redelivery** (`backoff.Policy`)
— exist but are (a) **modern-JetStream-only** and (b) **not yet consumed anywhere
in production**. Phase 2 deepens them so they can *replace* the proven production
implementations, while keeping the shared package's ownership narrow.

Surveys of the three reference repos pinned the exact contracts:

- **Legacy `nats.JetStreamContext` publishers** — entiredb `repoops` (`repo.ops.publish`)
  & `gitjobs` (`mirror.git.publish`), and mirror-pipeline `natspub` + its 6 typed
  publishers (`github_meta.publish`, …). All use `PublishMsg(m *nats.Msg, opts ...nats.PubOpt)`
  + `nats.Context(ctx)`, caller-selected span names, and the standard `messaging.*`
  attrs incl. `messaging.operation.type=publish` (which go-nuts' Publisher does **not**
  set today).
- **Modern `jetstream.JetStream` publishers** — entire-api `analysis` (no span today)
  & `forwarder` (full prologue, 5s bound) — already match `natsmsg.Publisher`.
- **Redelivery** — entiredb `repoops` (5s×2, cap **30s**, `MaxDeliver:-1`) & `permswebhook`
  (5s×2, cap = **configurable ceiling**, `-1`) and entire-api `ingest` (1s×2, cap **300s**,
  `MaxDeliver:8`) all use **modern `jetstream.Msg`**. The **only legacy `*nats.Msg`**
  redelivery consumer is mirror-pipeline `fanoutengine` (COR-762 Term-on-exhaustion,
  flat 30s Nak). entiredb's bit-shift `NakDelay << (N-1)` == `backoff` multiplicative
  `Factor:2` for the integer sequence (verified).

**User's stated goal: migrate everything to the modern interface.** So legacy support
is a *transitional bridge*; the modern API must be the pristine end state, and the

- **`backoff`** — the redelivery policy for transiently-failed deliveries: a
  `NakWithDelay` envelope — flat by default, optionally growing per delivery
  (`Factor`/`MaxDelay`) — bounded by MaxDeliver, with opt-in
  Term-on-final-delivery so a work-queue message is removed cleanly instead of
  orphaning un-acked. It owns disposition and delay calculation only, and drives
  both the modern `jetstream.Msg` API (`NakOrTerm`) and the legacy `*nats.Msg`
  API (`NakOrTermLegacy`). MaxDeliver mirrors `jetstream.ConsumerConfig`: a
  non-positive value (`0` or `UnlimitedMaxDeliver`) means unlimited redeliveries,
  so bridge an unset `jsconsumer` consumer with its `EffectiveMaxDeliver()`

Both P2 fixes are committed (`ac3f0ac`, checkpoint `3087f9932a47`) and pushed — PR [#10](https://github.com/entireio/go-nuts/pull/10) now includes them.

## What changed

**P2.1 — caller-owned span attributes preserved.** `Publisher.Publish` and `LegacyPublisher.Publish` now take a variadic `attrs ...attribute.KeyValue`, forwarded onto the internally-owned producer span through `StartProducerSpan` alongside the standard `messaging.*` set. So a Phase 3 replacement of mirror-pipeline's `natspub` (or the entiredb publishers) keeps its placement / job-identity tags **on the actual publish span** — no extra wrapping span, no topology change. The signature stays backward-compatible (existing zero-arg calls still compile).

**P2.2 — `messaging.operation.name` no longer misused.** I confirmed against the pinned semconv (`v1.41.0`): `operation.name` is the system-specific op (`send`/`ack`/`nack`), and the `operation.type` enum is `create/send/receive/process/settle`. The production implementations being replaced set `operation.type="publish"` (a valid low-cardinality custom value) and **no** `operation.name`. So I dropped `operation.name` entirely — the caller's `Operation` value is now the **span name only**, and `operation.type=publish` continues to carry the operation. This matches the production spans exactly (no added/changed attribute that would break existing dashboards) and stops leaking the app span name into the wrong semantic field.

The parity test now forwards domain attrs and asserts they land on the span while `messaging.operation.name` stays unset. All gates green again: `go test -race ./...`, `golangci-lint` (0 issues), gofmt, `go mod tidy -diff`, `git diff --check`.

The `v0.8.0` tag on `main` after merge remains the only open item.
